sampling_model.design: Independent superpopulation sampling with a randomized finite-support instrument conditional on each finite covariate stratum.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Conditional multinomial cell probabilities are empirical within \((x,z)\); finite-sample inversion uses cellwise Clopper--Pearson intervals and asymptotics use their multinomial influence vectors.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The paper learns deterministic categorical rules by minimizing a loss formed from coordinatewise action-mean intervals and explicitly leaves randomized rules for future development.
Proposition 1 characterizes all minimax allocations when every action-specific spike state is feasible.
Theorems 2 and 3 establish local asymptotic minimaxity of an empirical-success statistical treatment rule with many point-identified treatments under an asymptotically balanced sampling design.

Theorem 5.1 gives a binary stochastic policy whose treatment probability is formed from lower and upper bounds on a conditional treatment-effect contrast and improves the deterministic worst-case-regret bound.
Theorem 1 gives necessary and sufficient inequalities for compatibility of a full categorical-instrument counterfactual distribution.
Response functions and linear programming deliver tight symbolic bounds for finite causal models.
Randomized minimax regret over a finite uncertainty set is representable as a zero-sum linear program.
Random-right-hand-side linear programs have optimizer limits whose form depends on degeneracy and the selection rule.
Auxiliary linear programs yield limits and confidence sets for optimal solutions when the constraint matrix and objective are fixed and the right-hand side is random.
Directionally differentiable maps require derivative-aware inference and generally invalidate the ordinary bootstrap when full differentiability fails.
Criterion inversion constructs confidence regions for parameter sets defined by population minimization.
Local Gaussian limit experiments characterize asymptotically minimax treatment rules when partially identified bounds shrink at the root-n scale.

body.tldr: The headline result is a uniform sampling law for the population randomized minimax-regret rule when categorical-instrument cell probabilities move both the active saddle coefficients and the response-fiber right-hand side. An observable nondegenerate unique-face class stabilizes every response basis and KKT face, yields the derivative \(-E H^{-1}(DH)u\), and proves that the problem is not a fixed-matrix random-right-hand-side linear program. The response-function projection and finite randomized-regret composition are background. Supporting results give pure-rule and rectangularization certificates, an exact three-action rectangle-oracle separation, finite-sample correspondence coverage, and deployed-regret certification; uniform \(\sqrt n\)-contraction at intersecting faces remains open.

project_justification.gap: Random-linear-program limit theory fixes the constraint normals, while many-treatment statistical-rule theory studies repeated-sample decisions under point identification and existing partial-identification randomization formulas use binary marginal bounds. None gives fixed-law sampling inference for a categorical-instrument population mixture whose active regret normals change with the observed multinomial table.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is an observable active-system theory that tracks changes in the response-basis roster, active regret scenarios, policy support, and KKT coefficients before applying a delta method.
project_justification.fill: The paper states a nondegenerate unique-face margin class entirely in observable basis and KKT quantities, derives the moving-coefficient derivative and a uniform asymptotic linear representation, and proves a facet-normal obstruction to any fixed-matrix right-hand-side reduction. Exact set coverage and the three-action rectangle-oracle witness remain supporting consequences.

body.related_work: Manski2000TreatmentChoice separates treatment choice from point identification, and Stoye2007ManyTreatments supplies the spike-state population allocation benchmark recovered by Theorem 4. Masten2023ManyTreatmentRules studies statistical treatment rules that map experimental samples into allocations and proves local asymptotic minimaxity under point identification and asymptotically balanced designs; the target here is instead the fixed-law sampling distribution of a population mixed-action optimizer under partial identification. Cui2021PartialIDDecisions, Section 5.3 and Theorem 5.1, randomizes a binary action using marginal lower and upper bounds on a treatment-effect contrast; it does not optimize over three or more actions against the joint categorical-instrument response polytope or analyze the sampling law of that optimizer. SongEtAl2026CategoricalIV supplies the sharp compatible response-law set, SachsEtAl2023SymbolicBounds supplies response-function linear programming, and MastinJailletChin2014RandomizedRegret supplies the finite saddle template, so their composition is background. HruzaEtAl2026CategoricalPIL uses a deterministic coordinatewise-interval loss; Theorem 5 gives only an exact rectangle-oracle separation for its population benchmark. BonnansShapiro2000Perturbation informs the KKT margins. KlattMunkZemel2022RandomLP and LiuBuneaNilesWeed2023LPConfidence analyze fixed coefficient matrices with random right-hand sides, whereas Theorem 1 proves that the active categorical-instrument regret normals move. FangSantos2019DirectionalInference informs the open face-intersection handle. ClopperPearson1934Binomial and ChernozhukovHongTamer2007Sets inform the supporting finite-sample set inversion. MontielOleaQiuStoye2026Asymptotics studies a local Gaussian treatment-choice experiment rather than fixed-law inference for this population optimizer.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The presolve evidence was independently checked computationally but is not treated as proof. For the displayed witness, response-type filtering leaves twenty compatible columns; support-direction enumeration returns the ten stated projected vertices and the facets \(0\leq\mu_0\leq3/4\), \(1/4\leq\mu_1\leq3/4\), \(1/2\leq\mu_2\leq1\), and \(\mu_0\leq\mu_2\). Independent linear programs return \(q^\dagger=(0,1/4,3/4)\), \(v=3/16\), and the rectangle solution \((0,0,1)\), \(v^{\Box}=1/4\). The proof stage must reproduce these results by exact basis certificates and repeat the check under codimension-one perturbations; any omitted optimizer or false pure-rule certificate kills the angle.
body.honest_scope: The categorical-instrument response representation and its composition with a finite randomized-regret linear program are background ingredients, not the contribution. Theorem 1 is confined to the observable class on which all response bases and the unique primal--dual face are separated by fixed margins. Its fixed-matrix obstruction applies at laws where the observable projective-normal diagnostic is positive; the exceptional zero set is characterized rather than assumed away. The Gaussian result excludes face intersections. The Bonferroni set remains valid there without a contraction claim; uniformly honest \(\sqrt n\)-contraction at intersecting faces is the open-ended question.
